articleTitle: A Dual Primary Side FB DC-DC Converter with Variable Frequency Phase Shift Control Strategy for On/Off Board EV Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper deals with advanced version of L2C converter named it as iL2C (interleaved inductor-inductor-capacitor) converter for wide input voltage range of battery charging applications using dual primary side concept. It also introduces robust hybrid controller design called VFPSM strategy. The moto behind this study is to check the converter steady-state and transient performance during half load condition of full load i.e., 1.65 kW of 3.3 kW. The computer simulations are performed at rated input and output voltages of 400 Vin- 48 V0 and the dynamic performance of converter also discussed for 500 Vin to 300 Vin - 300 Vin to 500 Vin at 48 V0.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Dual Switch-Based Two Quadrant Bi-Polar DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a sixth-order bi-polar DC-DC converter (SOBPDC) that is capable of smoothly varying the voltage gain with duty ratio and providing an output voltage of either polarity. The proposed converter is an enhancement of a conventionally modified bi-polar converter that includes a feature for a high voltage conversion ratio while minimizing the number of controlled switches required. The SOBPDC operates in either bi-polar mode based on the power demanded by the load and energy requirements. When the duty ratio is less than 0.38, the SOBPDC provides positive output voltage with the bucking operation. Conversely, the SOBPDC utilizes buck-boosting operation at high-duty ratios to generate a negative output voltage. A mathematical model of the proposed converter and a comparative analysis has been conducted. The simulation study of A 48 V to ±36 V, 50 kHz is carried out and presented to validate the proposed converter's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Solar PV Array based Grid-Connected Bi-Directional EV Charger Controlled using NARLMMN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new Normalised Adaptive Regression Least Mean Mixed Norm (NARLMMN) algorithm to control three phase Voltage Source Converter (VSC). Further, the paper considers an On-Board EV Charger and a PV source connected at DC link of the VSC. The PV feeds real power to Electric Vehicle (EV) and the grid. Both the Grid to Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) operations are implemented using bidirectional Buck-Boost converter which is an emergent area of research. The grid supplies power to charge the battery of EV in G2V mode of operation. In V2G mode of operation, the stored energy in the EV battery bank is reutilized to supply back to the utility grid, which helps in peak shaving, load balancing, voltage management and improving the system reliability. The bidirectional DC-DC converter, along with the battery bank are connected at the DC link of three phase VSC and controlled to implement charging and discharging modes. The performance of PV with VSC and PV, EV with VSC is analysed on MATLAB/Simulink platform. The PWM control technology is used to regulate the voltage and current used for charging and discharging batteries. The dynamics of the proposed system are analyzed and results are shown in this paper with the new proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Improved Power Quality for On-Board EV Charger with a Cascaded Dual-Active Bridge Power Factor Correction Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a Boost Power Factor Corrector (PFC) integrated with a high-frequency isolated Dual Active Bridge converter (BPFC-DAB) for onboard Electric Vehicle (EV) charging applications. When an EV charges from the AC grid, the AC-DC converter behaves as a non-linear load, thus drawing intermittent peaky currents that lead to a significant decrease in the input power factor. Thus, enhancing the power factor can assist in penalty avoidance, which will be assured by a Boost PFC unit with dual-loop PI control. This conditioned DC power is then fed to the battery using a Dual Active Bridge (DAB), which electrically isolates the grid and the EV. This improves safety and enables fast charging using variable voltage with higher power density. To achieve the aforementioned objectives, a small-signal model for the proposed charger has been obtained to tune the close-loop PI gains of both cascaded converters using the frequency domain approach. The presented methodology with its control has been validated through simulations and verified using a 2.2kW hardware prototype with 230V AC input, 350V DC link voltage, and 450V output for battery charging.

articleTitle: Decoupled Control of Single-Input Double-Output Boost-Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper proposes a modified single-input double-output boost-flyback converter and its decoupling control technique. The converter avails two different outputs i.e. one to supply a light load at low-voltage and another to supply heavier load at higher voltage in single-stage itself. The availability of different voltage/power outputs is need of toady's automation in power applications such as in personal computers, electric vehicles, smart grids, shipboards. The major challenges of the coupled-inductor or flyback transformer-based multi-output converter are cross-coupling and cross-regulation issues. The proposed converter not only supplies two different outputs but also eliminate coupling and regulation issues. Moreover, the low voltage/power output of converter remains isolated from higher voltage/power output. The working principle of proposed converter and its PWM scheme, dynamic model and a procedure to find decoupling condition to design a decoupled control technique are discussed. Also, to verify the working of converter and its decoupled-control the simulation results are presented using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Single Stage Isolated AC/DC LLC Resonant Power Conversion Stage with Reduced Current/Voltage Stress for Light EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The operation of PFC stage in hard-switching is quite common, which reduces overall conversion efficiency in two stage EV chargers. To cater this issue, a single stage direct AC/DC LLC resonant converter based EV charger design is presented in this paper. Converter utilizes interleaved concept at grid end and each interleaved phase realizes only half of grid voltage. This effective implementation reduces voltage stress across MOSFETs for its discontinuous interleaved inductor current mode (DIICM) operation. DICM design features small passive footprints and easy control implementation. A time weighted average designing (TWAD) design ensures zero voltage switching (ZVS) with reduced turn-off switching losses. Additionally, with DICM of interleaved state and TWAD design of LLC tank parameters, single charging current control loop provides DC link boost capability with charging current tracking. A O.5kW EV charger is designed to validate TWAD design technique and single stage AC/DC power converter.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Solid State Circuit Breaker for DC System using Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Relative to solid-state circuit breakers that utilizes IGBTs and MOSFETs, the thyristor-based circuit breakers offer greater capacity and affordability, making them suitable for use as solid state breaker for higher power DC supply system. Nonetheless, recently the thyristor-based circuit breakers faced limitations towards reliably interrupting of fault currents during high resistance faults. To address this, a new and efficient circuit breaker is introduced in this paper, designed to accomplish automatic and controllable turn-off operations. The fault current through a coupled inductor is used to increase the capacitor voltage which turns-off the main switch. A fast acting switch is utilized to reduce the time of operation. This proposed configuration amalgamates the benefits of high efficiency, rapid responsiveness, and dependability. The effectiveness of the proposed circuit breaker is verified through MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation at a power rating of 25 kW DC system.

articleTitle: Optimal DG Allocation for Maximizing Operational Benefits in Unbundled Electric Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple and effective model for optimally placing the distributed generations (DGs) in an unbundled paradigm of an electric distribution system. The proposed framework aims to maximize the operational benefits of both the distribution company (DistCo) and distributed generation owners (DGOs). The formulated mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem is subject to equality constraints given by DistFlow equations for power balance and inequality constraints in the form of upper and lower limits on decision variables. This optimization process deliberates the hourly variation of load demand and electricity price to approximate the daily operations. The proposed model is tested on a well-known radial distribution network (i.e., 33-bus), illustrating different case studies and verifying the efficacy. The numerical results show improvement in the distribution network's physical condition after placing the DGs optimally.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Analysis of Active Distribution Network Based on Rate of Change of Frequency using RTDS and PMUs
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research analyzes the fault identification mechanisms for active distribution networks (ADNs) based on the Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF) approach using Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS). The duration of the outage can be shortened by accurately identifying the distribution system's fault. This will help in the recovery process and system restoration. Due to the incorporation of renewable energy sources and the existence of power electronic devices, ADNs have grown more sophisticated. It is likely that distribution networks are going to witness considerable and arbitrary DG penetration given the current trend of embracing and integrating renewable energy and microgrids. As a result, distribution systems will become multisource imbalanced systems, where preventive devices may fail to operate together. Therefore, for dependable and effective operation, improved fault detection and protection mechanisms are needed. The suggested technique uses RTDS's high-speed simulation capabilities and PMUs precise frequency measurements to create a fault identification mechanism that is effective and based on ROCOF analysis. With encouraging positive results, the approach has been thoroughly tested on an IEEE 13-bus distribution system integrated with the DG, for open and short circuit faults on all zones of the system.

articleTitle: Implementation and Operation of Hybrid Multilevel and Multipulse Power Converter for High-Performance of Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: One of most important research topics in induction motor drive configurations applied to medium voltage applications is power quality analysis, circuit complexity, and efficiency profile. This research work describes a hybrid six-level converter based on a neutral point clamped converter and cascaded two-level voltage source inverter suitable structure for medium voltage application of industry. Exhibited high-power hybrid converter ensures high power quality at motor terminal of the drive system. Furthermore, a thirty-pulse multipulse AC-DC converter is designed and implemented, which supplies power at DC-link terminal of hybrid inverter as well as improves power quality performance at input terminal of drive system. Secondary winding of multi-winding transformer is designed with phase displacement technique; due to this, harmonic components injected to grid by one rectifier are canceled out by harmonic components of other rectifiers. Feasibility of exhibited power converter circuit for induction motor drive systems is verified by computer simulation for a 400hp induction motor.

articleTitle: A Self-Reliant 3P4W Grid-Interfaced, Single-Stage, PVEG-BES System with DSTATCOM Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The objective of this investigation is to realise a utility interfaced, three-phase, four-wire, photovoltaic energy generation-battery energy storage (PVEG-BES) system capable of supplying loads connected at common point of interface with ability to inject surplus available power as an active power to utility mains. Modified Voltage and current based perturbation technique monitors maximum power point tracking even with simultaneous variation in load and irradiation. A reduced order generalised differentiator (ROGD) methodology is used to extract the fundamental weight component of load current. The voltage source converter in grid-following mode functions as a multi-functional device that provides reactive power demand of non-linear loads locally, compensates for current harmonics through neutral line and maintains grid current sinusoidal with suitable power quality indices on supply side. The system controller enables seamless transition between islanded mode and grid connected mode. For islanding/auto re-synchronisation with three-phase utility, reduced-order generalised differentiator-frequency locked loop (ROGD-FLL) is put to use which effectively measures amplitude, frequency, and phase in accordance with IEEE-1547. A proper power management methodology is incorporated in this investigation to prevent the BES system from being overcharged/deep discharged. The system is realised in MATLAB environment in discrete time frame using simulink and sim power system toolboxes. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of grid current in grid-following mode and load voltage in grid forming mode are within range as per IEEE- 519 and 929 respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Symmetrical Multilevel Inverter Topology With Reduced Number of Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Multilevel inverters are useful for obtaining a high-quality AC output with reduced Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) values. It is evident that the increased inverter output levels demand the high number of switching devices and multiple DC sources, leading to an escalation in the size and complexity of the circuit. This paper proposes a novel circuit topology for Symmetrical Multilevel Inverters (SMIs) to address the issues associated with increased number of switching devices like switching losses, cost, circuit and control complexities. In this paper, it is proposed to combine a diode-clamped inverter with an H-bridge inverter. This combination reduces the requirement of switching devices and the connected issues such as the losses and inverter complexities.

articleTitle: An Autonomous AC Microgrid Controlled by Active Disturbance Rejection Control in a Master-slave Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, a microgrid based on master-slave topology is presented and controlled using an improved Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADCR) strategy. The presented control scheme consists of two loops, where the outer loop controls the voltage at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC), while the inner loop is responsible for controlling the injected current to the connected loads at the PCC. ADRC is a controller that has a feedback controller, which is a Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller, and an Extended State Observer (ESO) that can estimate both external and internal uncertainties of the system by only using a partial knowledge of the system dynamics; hence, it is a suitable controller for the microgrid system. The proposed strategy is compared to the performance of a Proportional-Integral (PI) scheme to illustrate its meritorious performance. Simulation results show that the ADRC highly enhances the system's performance.

articleTitle: Designing a Fuzzy Logic Controller for Soft-Switched Quadratic Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper introduces of successful implementation of fuzzy logic controller (FLC) structure for an active clamp-coupled inductor-based soft-switched Quadratic Boost Converter. This proposed method aims to address several key challenges, including low sensitivity to input voltage variation, fast regulation during load transients, and robustness against aging effects on the converter's passive components. To solve all these issues a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is designed, it is stated that utilizing a convergent distribution for the membership function leads to a faster response compared to symmetrically distributed membership functions. The robustness of the controller is evaluated under varying loading conditions and input voltage variations. Furthermore, the results are compared with conventional controllers (PI), showing superior dynamic performance. Simulink/ MATLAB is used to validate the performance of the controller.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement of Synchronous Reluctance Generator Based Standalone Distributed System Utilizing Universal Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work demonstrates the performance of a synchronous reluctance generator (SyRG) based distributed power generation system (DPGs) using a universal active filter (UAF). The AC source for both linear and nonlinear loads is a SyRG generator. With the incorporation of UAF for SyRG-based standalone DPGs, the power factor at source terminals is improved. UAF's parallel-connected voltage source converter (VSC) injects harmonics currents to ensure balanced and sinusoidal source currents. Series connected VSC of UAF injects voltage to compensate for any voltage drop or distortion in generation. A model is developed in MATLAB/Simulink to analyze the efficacy of PQ enhancement in various situations and obtained results are discussed. Qualities of voltages across sensitive loads and current qualities at generator terminals are simultaneously enhanced and ensure to follow the IEEE standard 519 using UAF.

articleTitle: Three Phase Charging System using Grid to Vehicle and Vehicle to Grid Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The research study presents a complex system that uses cutting-edge converters to control energy transfer. It is called Grid to Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle to Grid (V2G). A three-phase bidirectional AC-DC converter and a DC-DC buck-boost converter are used in the arrangement. A bidirectional AC-DC converter is used in the G2V process to transform a 415V, 50 Hz AC power source into an 800V DC output, guaranteeing a sinusoidal current and unity power factor. On the other hand, during V2G, the vehicle's batteries' stored energy can be returned to the power grid, helping to stabilize the entire power system. The DC-DC buck-boost converter has two functions: it functions as a boost converter during battery discharge and as a buck converter during battery charging. PI controllers are used to regulate the charging and discharging procedures with regard to voltage and current. The study demonstrates the efficacy of the suggested algorithm through simulations, demonstrating the system's usefulness in realistic applications. Offering a viable option for bidirectional energy transfer between electric vehicles and the power grid, this cutting-edge device demonstrates the potential for improved energy management and grid stability.

Author Keywords: three phase Full Bridge AC-DC Converter

articleTitle: Modular Battery Balancing and Power Flow Management Using Isolated Multi-Port DC-DC Converter with Active Power Sharing Control
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper describes a Modular Multiport Converter (MMC), including an active charge balancing unit with isolated power converters while achieving the desired power exchange between the multi-ports of a common AC-link hybrid converter. The MMC includes multiple battery modules connected to individual H-bridges and interfaced to the common high-frequency AC link. The AC link consists of a multi-winding high-frequency transformer with multiple primary windings for the battery module H-bridges and a secondary winding for in-terfacing Electric Vehicle (EV) loads through another secondary H-bridge converter. The MMC control strategy includes a hybrid control approach, where active charge balance is achieved amongst the battery modules based on their State-of-Charge (SOC) using a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) control. The individual duty ratios of the input-side H-bridges are selected for the active charge balancing based on their respective SOC levels. The hybrid control approach includes a single-phase shift control for achieving bi-directional power exchange between the input-side H-bridges and the secondary H-bridge while maintaining the EV terminal voltage. The effectiveness of the topology is validated using the PLECS simulation tool by analysing different battery packs and varying load and charging conditions with the proposed closed-loop control.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ANFIS and PI Based Control of DFIG for Wind Power Generation with Grid-Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper provides a comparative control strategy analysis for a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind energy conversion system (WECS) in grid-connected mode, and its comparative analysis to a conventional PI controller and an adaptive neuro-fuzzy interface system(ANFIS). It is developed to regulate the speed of rotor side converters and the grid side converter in DFIG-WECS grid-connected operation. The proposed approach performs better under different load conditions and wind speeds by keeping a constant output voltage. The flux alignment is assured by the ANFIS management of the rotor side converter and compared with the PI controller. As the rotation of the turbine varies with wind speed, the supply frequency to the load is kept constant using the ANFIS control. Also, ANFIS performs more robustly in keeping the DC link voltage of the capacitor interconnected between rotor side and grid side converter compared to a PI controller. The simulation outcomes demonstrate the controller's exceptional performance due to its robust control over supply frequency and load voltage when wind speed fluctuates with nonlinear load demand.

articleTitle: Selection of The Power MOSFET in The Zeta Converter Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, selection of power semiconductor in the static converter not only depends on the manufacturer specifications but also depends on the operating characteristics when the MOSFET uses for the static converter application. Various case study and modeling of the static power converter have been discussed by the parameters of power MOSFET how to play the parasitic components of its equivalent circuit in the converter topology as objective of the paper

articleTitle: Sub-Synchronous Resonance Mitigation in Series-Compensated Power Systems Using a GWO-Based Optimal Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper uses a GWO-based optimum controller to dampen sub-synchronous resonance in a series-compensated power system network. The research was conducted using the IEEE's original benchmark model. Traditionally, a static var system (SVS)'s connection to a lengthy transmission line has been assumed to occur near the line's middle. The optimal controller considers all the system's different states as feedback to stabilize the outputs. On the test system, an Eigenvalue analysis was performed with the help of a linearized system model in order to enhance the system's stability and decrease the frequency of sub-synchronous oscillations. In this study, we investigate and compare the effectiveness of the optimal controller, optimal controller with BFOA, and optimal controller with GWO for damping the electromechanical torsional oscillations in a specific series compensated power system. The effectiveness of the proposed damping strategy is demonstrated via a time-domain method based on dynamic response.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control Strategy for Rapid Charging of Electric Vehicle Battery Pack
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Quick electric vehicle (EV) charging has become essential for widespread EV adoption but poses challenges, notably in the degradation of lithium-ion batteries, irrespective of physical limitations. To address the above-mentioned issue, this paper presents Modified Enhanced Horse Herd Optimization (MHHO) technology, designed to fasten and optimize battery charging. The MHHO approach was rigorously evaluated through simulations to assess its feasibility and suitable outcomes. The results demonstrated its potential to significantly reduce battery charging durations while maintaining operational efficiency. Crucially, this approach incorporates real-time control mechanisms to ensure that the charging process adheres to safe temperature and voltage parameters.

articleTitle: Supervisory Control of an Inverter-based Microgrid Using PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Microgrid supervisory control is essential for inverter-based microgrid operation. This paper uses the PSO Algorithm, a nature-inspired optimization method, to supervise an inverter-based microgrid. The PSO Algorithm efficiently searches the solution space to discover the optimum control strategy that minimizes voltage and frequency error, maximizes renewable energy integration, and improves grid stability while fulfilling operational limitations. The study deals with establishing the objective function, mapping optimized solutions to control error, and coordinating control actions for microgrid operation. Simulations show that PSO optimization outperforms conventional microgrid control methods.

articleTitle: Performance Study on A Small-Scale Solar and Wind Based DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Direct Current Microgrids (MGs) have become increasingly popular as a means of delivering reliable as well as efficient power to remote areas, such as residential loads, educational institutions, and health centres. These Direct current (DC) MGs include various energy generation sources such as solar photovoltaic (SPV), wind energy generation (WTG), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and controllable grid-tied electric vehicles (EVs). In addition, the usage of compact fluorescent lights (CFL), light-emitting diode (LED) bulbs, refrigerators, TVs, fans, air conditioners, laptops, and other devices in homes and workplaces is constantly increasing the DC loads in buildings. In order to supply electricity to remote residential areas, this research proposes a 48 V standalone DC MG that operates only in grid-connected under various conditions. The primary objective of this work is to implement a domestic-level DC MG in rural and remote areas which utilizes renewable energy sources (RES). The proposed DC MG was designed and simulated successfully for various loads using suitable power electronic converters. The proposed DC MG's performance and control method are validated using the MATLAB Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of High Voltage PMSM Drive with Bidirectional Converter for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained significant popularity in recent years due to their environmental benefits, energy efficiency, motor control and advancements in battery technology. This paper presents sensorless vector control of high voltage permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) utilizing bidirectional DC-DC converter. Bidirectional DC-DC converter helps to provide high voltage required DC link voltage from a low voltage battery as well as reverse power flow during braking condition. In addition to this, mechanical sensorless technique based on sliding mode observer with cascaded second order generalized integrator (CSOGI) is employed for rotor position and speed estimation. CSOGI effectively suppress harmonics present in back-EMF as well as DC- off set from both in phase as well as quadrature component, which improves sensorless speed and position estimation. Furthermore, to migrate disturbance and fluctuation caused due to current sensor measurement error, cogging torque and inverter nonlinearity, proportional integral in parallel with resonant controller (PIR) based speed controller is utilized for closed loop vector control. Topology analysis, controller performance and its comparison are implemented and verified with obtained results.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Boost, Cuk and Zeta PFC Converters in Continuous Current Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of boost, Cuk and Zeta converters in power factor correction (PFC) mode of working in continuous current operation. The various parameters of power quality performance and power factor correction for different topologies of converters at source side have been studied. All three converters have been simulated in closed loop control for the heating loads with current controlled heating.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of 17-Level Converter with New Level Generation Unit for Large-Scale Solar Plant in Environmental Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a new level generation unit based seventeen level power inverter for solar applications. It utilizes lesser switches as compared to well-known H bridge based topology. Each module utilizes only six switches and four modules adds up to have 17 levels in the phase voltage. A transformer-less approach is shown with proper power tracking and controller methodology. The operating modes shows the level development for each state. Closed implementation is done with control approach in different irradiance conditions. The power flow is regulated with the help of proportional resonant controllers. Fundamental switching is done to have minimum losses in the conversion. By introducing the real power component, the controller both ensures unit power factor operation and elevates the grid's performance. The converter dynamics are recorded in different dynamic conditions and the presented results are validated with real-time test bench. The temperature variations are also shown to showcase the effect of temperature on converter performance. This new converter is tested for harmonic performance, which shows that it is ideal for grid integration and follows the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Study of Various Power Converter Topologies in a Common Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, study of various power converter topologies have been concentrated by a common platform for the designing corridor. Theory, designing maturity, modeling and simulation of various power converter topologies have been extended as big support of the converter fabrication and supply chain management in the corridor of high frequency switching power supplies with advanced power semiconductors as objective of the paper

articleTitle: Optimum Torque Operation of a Hybrid Cascaded Multilevel Converter-Fed Electric Vehicle Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper describes a Hybrid Cascaded Multilevel Converter (HCMC) used in Electric Vehicles (EV) for motoring and extracting optimal power during regenerative braking operations. The HCMC converter includes a T-type inverter connected to an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) interfaced with a common DC link. A battery is connected to the DC link using a bi-directional boost converter. The control structure of the HCMC system includes two cascaded dual-loop control structures. The dual-loop control architecture of the IPMSM motor includes inner current control loops and an outer speed control loop. Further, the dual-loop structure of the battery-connected boost converter includes an inner average inductor/battery current control loop and an outer DC link regulator loop. A heuristic Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) Look-up-Table (LUT)-based methodology is adopted for the IPMSM inner control loops that generate optimized direct and quadrature-axes current references for the motoring mode. Further, optimum energy recovery is achieved with maximum regenerative torque during the braking mode. The IPMSM inverter is controlled using a three-level Space Vector Modulation (SVM) scheme for the T-type inverter. The direct axis current reference for the IPMSM inner loop is modulated based on the required reluctance torque using MTPA methodology. The technique proposed here is verified using PLECS simulation and presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Performance Improvement Through SPRS Using Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research paper presents the effectiveness of induction motor with wound rotor drive that employs a slip power recovery scheme (SPRS) using a five-level inverter and buck-boost chopper and LC filter is being used. Capacitor clamped inverter using insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) and a buck-boost chopper control approach employing metal-oxide-semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs) as switching devices with an LC filter. A mathematical model for 2hp, 400V, 50Hz, 1440 rpm induction motor drive (IMD) has been simulated in MATLAB environment. Total harmonic distortion (THD) and power factor of supply are taken as performance parameters for the analysis. The suggested technique is unique because, it implements the SPRS simulation model utilizing a five-level inverter and a buck-boost chopper. The simulation results suggest that a five-level inverter with chopper control and an LC filter reduces THD, as a result power quality of system gets improved.

articleTitle: Design & Analysis of Self Tuning Filter for Phase Locked Loop Under Weak Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The phase-locked loop (PLL) determines the grid voltage's phase angle and frequency by generating synchronising signals. This paper proposes a self-tuning filter (STF) phase-locked loop (PLL) to improve power quality in weak grid conditions, generate synchronising signals, and calculate the magnitude of supply voltage. Under weak grid conditions, there are problems with current-based and voltage-based power quality. Phase-locked loops (PLL) are widely employed for synchronisation and tracking parameters such as frequency and phase angle. This paper proposes STF-PLL, which is utilised to solve voltage-based problems: voltage sag and swell, voltage harmonics, DC offset, grid phase angle fluctuations, and frequency. This study has compared the results of STF-PLL to the conventional algorithms: SRF (synchronous reference frame)-PLL and DSOGI (double second order generalised integrator)-PLL. When the supply voltage is given as input, the proposed controller generates synchronising signals and computes the magnitude of the supply voltage. STF-PLL algorithm provides better response characteristics, smoother frequency, and phase change, which makes it a better algorithm.

articleTitle: 3 C, 4 C Topology for Wireless Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In recent times, wireless charging is challenging wired charging in terms of flexibility, convenience, safety, and the capability of becoming fully automated. The research is taking place on various compensation topologies that is an essential component of wireless charging. This article proposes 3-C topology, 4-C topology for compensation required in wireless electric vehicle charging. The main focus is to develop the load independent topology that is free from inductor. In addition, constant current output is achieved by this topology. The 2-coil arrangement is treated as transformer. The relation is derived between the coil arrangement and transformer model. The simulation model is applied to various resistive load values to check independence. The source current is observed for both 3 C topology, 4 C topology and later also compared with LCC topology. The voltage stress across various capacitors used in compensation is also observed.

articleTitle: Data Decomposition Strategy to Improve Solar Forecasting Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: One of the key tasks for the planning, balancing, and management of the grid is an accurate estimate of solar irradiation. The solar global horizontal irradiance (GHI) is intermittent to the climatic characteristics and geographical locations. Therefore, two deep learning (DL) models: (Long short-term memory (LSTM) and Gated recurrent unit (GRU), are developed in this study to forecast accurate and precise solar GHI. Furthermore, to examine the impact of signal processing approach on accuracy, the LSTM and GRU are also used in combination with the complete ensemble empirical mode for decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN). The CEEMDAN decomposes the dataset to decompose in to several intrinsic mode functions (IMF) and improve the learning ability of LSTM and GRU. As a results, it is observed that the decomposition technique improves the forecasting accuracy by reducing the forecasting errors (RMSE: 31% and MAE: 40%).

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic-Enhanced EV Battery Charging Station: Integration of Solar PV, SEPIC and Buck Converter with MPPT Based CC-CV Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The designing and modeling of renewable based Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS), using Solar Photovoltaics (SPV), SEPIC converter along with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control, a BUCK converter as Voltage Regulation (VR) mechanism and Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV) battery control for Li-ion battery charging which here is assumed as EV battery is proposed. A detailed modeling of the system is done in MATLAB/SIMULINK. The increase in Electric Vehicle (EV) has led to increasing demand of EVCS. The design proposed here is for off grid standalone charging station with renewable source integration enhancing green and clean energy source for sustainable transportation. Standalone systems are required to power the charging stations where grid feasibility is not available like in rural areas. SEPIC along with MPPT algorithm is used to dynamically optimize operating points of SPV to achieve maximum energy under different environmental conditions. In this paper a sustainable power generation system for Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS) is proposed. The adoption of FLC for CC-CV control is advantageous over PID control in dealing with nonlinearities and adapting real time conditions parameters in changing environment. The performance and feasibility of system is demonstrated via results of simulations in SIMULINK. The dynamic responses of FLC based CC-CV charging system and overall system is observed.

articleTitle: Vehicle to Grid Technologies Resolving Micro Grid Power Intermittencies Issues
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Electric vehicle energy storage system are valuable power asset in a modern Grid system. With electric vehicles to Grid integration sustainable energy management get achieved with improved stability and Power management capabilities in a micro-grid architecture. Implementation of V2G integration using fast off-board Level-3 bidirectional charging circuitry in a modelled micro-grid addressing power variation issues due to intermittent renewable power generation is presented in this paper. Simulation Analysis is performed evaluating dynamic response and stability of V2G operations. The test results conveys importance of V2G integration in regulating Grid power and dc bus voltage at rated values during disturbances. The vehicles supplies power to grid and regulates active power flow during renewable power intermittencies. The converters, controllers and filters ensures minimum harmonic distortion of injected Grid current and proving improved dynamic stability.

articleTitle: Single Solution for Control and Synchronization of Inverters in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The primary focus of this paper is to propose the control and synchronization of inverter usage in microgrids. The crucial issues in the parallel operation of inverters are accurate proportional load sharing and voltage control. A well-known droop technique has been employed widely due to its simple structure & wireless control. This manuscript focuses on limitations of conventional droop control (CDC) and and its remedial measures through bolting regulator on its control loop. Further efforts have been made to incorporate synchronization mechanism into the droop control by resembling its structure with Phase locked loop (PLL). Small signal stability analysis is also presented to ensure stable steady state operation. A comparison of output voltages, shared power ratios have been made for unequal per unit internal impedances of parallel operated R inverters (equipped with and without regulator) through the time domain simulations.

articleTitle: Estimation of State of Health of Li-Ion Batteries using Data Driven Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Battery health is a critical factor influencing the widespread adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs). The SoH serves as a reliable indicator of a battery's capacity degradation over time, directly impacting its performance and overall lifespan. In this research paper, various ensemble based techniques have been used to estimate the state of Health (SoH) of battery. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a detailed comparison of several state-of-the-art regression models is conducted. Specifically, the performance of Bagging Regression, Gradient Boost Model, Stacking Regression Model, xGBoost Model, and Extra Trees Model is evaluated in predicting the SoH of batteries. R-squared (R2) score is utilized as the metric for assessing the accuracy and predictive capability of the developed models. The performance of the developed models are evaluated using progressively reduced amounts of data, demonstrating its effectiveness even with limited available data. Through extensive analysis of the developed models, efficacy of the data-driven technique is demonstrated in estimating battery SoH accurately. Certain models outperform others in terms of R2 score, indicating superior predictive capabilities for battery health estimation. The results offer valuable insights for selecting the most suitable regression model for battery SoH estimation, contributing to enhanced EV battery management and optimization.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network for Chaotic Wind Speed Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting is essential for wind energy systems, but it's difficult due to the wind's uncertainty. In this study, short-time wind speed prediction is done on the basis of phase space reconstruction and using neural network techniques. The NREL (National Renewable Energy Laboratory) site collects the wind speed data. Firstly, the chaotic nature of the time series is ascertained to verify its short time predictability. Then training data is created by using the phase space reconstruction technique, i.e., using knowledge of embedding delay and embedding dimension. Using this data, two models of Artificial neural networks, i.e., Feedforward neural network (FFNN) and Recurrent Neural network (RNN) are trained to predict wind speed. Training accuracy of each model is compared on the basis of Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) & Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) metrics. Simulation results show the superiority of RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) over FFNN (Feed Forward Neural Network) for the prediction of wind speed.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Induction Motor with Advanced Capacitor Braking Using Adaptive Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In induction machines, the predominant challenge has been the significant temperature rise, which determines the state of maximum loading. The paramount objective is to achieve optimal capacitive braking, ensuring swift motor deceleration with minimal heat generation, thus highly applicable in scenarios necessitating frequent and rapid stops. This study presents an advanced braking scheme for threephase induction motors, effectively remedying the limitations of conventional capacitor braking systems. Consequently, the need for a complex and extensively explored multi-stage braking strategy, previously employed by numerous scholars, is obviated. The thorough analysis encompasses diverse parameters such as torque, braking time, and terminal capacitance. Power flow calculations scrutinize transient and steady-state braking, encompassing the power transfer from the input terminal to the shaft. The thermal consequences and effects on winding parameters due to sudden braking are also meticulously examined within the Simulink environment. The braking system's performance is evaluated, while a neural network estimates the efficacy limit of capacitive braking. This comprehensive paper encompasses electrical and thermal modelling and implements an enhanced capacitor braking mechanism for induction motors in Simulink.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Composite Controller for Alleviating Chaotic Oscillations in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper discusses the alleviation of chaotic oscillations in a power system and its impact on large-scale interconnected power grids. Conventional composite controller method using intelligent techniques is analyzed. A 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order model is employed to represent the power system with numerical algorithms capable of identifying chaotic motion in complex mathematical models, investigating catastrophic voltage collapse in chaotic power systems, and possible controllers with intelligent control techniques to extinguish chaos in practical applications. The chaotic system (CSGIB: chaotic single-generator infinite-bus) comprises an alternator parallel to an infinite bus. The chaotic behavior can arise with a certain set of system parameters. The suppression of chaos is done by various intelligent techniquesbased composite controllers in a reasonable time frame. Where the PSO (particle swarm optimization)-based composite controller exhibits the optimal results.

articleTitle: CHB-STATCOM Implemented with an Improved Virtual Synchronous Machine Controller with Adaptive Virtual Inertia
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Control of virtual synchronous generators, also known as synchronverter control, is gaining prominence as an effective method for integrating renewable energy sources into utility grids or microgrids. This control technique emulates the response of a traditional synchronous generator, leading to enhanced system stability. This paper presents the design of a controller for a cascaded H-bridge based Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM), inspired by the concept of a virtual synchronous machine. The controller is developed based on the mathematical model of synchronous generators operating in the compensator mode. An additional operation, droop control mode is implemented in the operation of the STATCOM. This mode is introduced alongside the standard voltage regulation mode and the direct reactive power control mode. This enables the appropriate sharing of reactive power across parallel-operated STATCOM. This study presents a novel approach for adaptive virtual inertia control by utilising an enhanced bang-bang control method.

articleTitle: KAMMA Gear Flywheel Hybrid Perpetual Mechanical Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: KAMMA Gear Flywheel Power Plant generates pure, clean and green energy, multiplies it and stores the energy. KAMMA Flywheel technology produces uninterrupted green electricity without use of raw material during its operational state. KAMMA Flywheel technology emits no harmful gases into the atmosphere hence it works in compliance with Net Zero Carbon Emission Norms. KAMMA Flywheel technology is the one and only eco-friendly power generation method in the world.

Author Keywords: Pulse based acceleration and deceleration methos
Hybrid perpetual mechanical battery techniques and technologies

articleTitle: Single Stage 3P4W for Grid Interfaced Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper deals with a multifunctional 3P4W (Three Phase Four Wire) grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system with a single-stage topology using QSS-LMS (Quadratic Step Size Least Mean Square) control. A grid tied VSC with this proposed control facilitates several functions to enhance power quality in the distribution grid such as harmonics reduction, grid currents balancing, and grid neutral current elimination. Simulated and test results show a satisfactory performance of 3P4W grid fed PV system under load unbalancing and variable solar insolation levels. THDs (Total Harmonics Distortions) of grid currents are observed well are well below 5% limit.

articleTitle: Mechanical Position Sensor-Less Torque Control of SRM With Reduced Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on a technique for reducing the cost and enhancing the performance and reliability of a switched reluctance motor (SRM). Specifically, it explores a current sensor reduction method for an SRM that operates using the fundamental switching of a midpoint converter. This configuration necessitates the incorporation of four current sensors for all the four phases. The implementation of the torque sharing function (TSF) based direct instantaneous torque control is utilized to minimize torque ripple and to implement current sensors reduction. The current sensing technique employed in this study utilizes a single neutral current sensor together with two sensors for each pair of phase windings and the TSF commutation angles. To enhance the reliability of the drive position sensorless control, an improved observer-based estimation method is used to estimate the rotor position and the speed. The flux linkage-based position estimation scheme utilizes the reconstructed currents for estimating the rotor position. Presented combined current and position sensor reduction method uses a four-phase, eight/six switched reluctance motor (SRM) to assess the viability through simulation findings.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Interleaved DC-DC Buck Converter for Li-Ion Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The charging infrastructure plays a crucial role in the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) by providing accessible, convenient, and technologically compatible charging solutions to extend the driving range and contribute to environmental sustainability. The DC-DC converters and their control are essential components utilized in charging infrastructure with efficient conversion of input voltage to optimal levels. This paper presents the design and implementation of an interleaved DC-DC buck converter for Lithium-ion battery charging applications. The incorporation of interleaving in the DC-DC buck converter enhances the overall both system performance. The interleaved architecture eliminates the need for inter-converter communication and effectively avoids any potential single point of failure. To achieve controlled and regulated output voltage, closed-loop control algorithm is implemented in TMS320F28027 microcontroller. The hardware of the interleaved DC-DC buck converter is tested on resistive load as well as on 48 V, 30 Ah Li-ion battery. The charging of the 48 V, 30 Ah Li-ion battery is carried out in Constant Current-Constant Voltage (CC-CV) mode. The experimental result of the developed interleaved DC-DC buck converter is presented in this work.

articleTitle: Environmental Emission Based Multi-objective Economic Dispatch Scheduling with Demand Flexibility in Micro-grid
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents an optimized framework for multi-objective environmental emission based economic generation schedule with demand flexibility in micro-grid. The environmental pollution produced by conventional generators is a major problem in power system operation. Economic scheduling of generators optimizes only cost without any concern on emissions. Multi-objective economic emission dispatch optimizes the cost and emission in a compromised manner. Paradigm is changing in modern power system with management from demand side. Demand flexibility provides an optimal scheduling by balancing load demand and generation of various generators. Renewable energy sources like wind turbine generators and photo-voltaic module are main generation sources in micro-grid. In this paper, test system with three conventional generators, a wind turbine generator and a photo-voltaic module has been proposed. Two scenarios have been presented with and without renewable energy sources. Demand flexibility effects on cost and emission demonstrates the effectiveness of management from demand side. Multi-objective economic dispatch results shows the improvement considering all sources and considering all sources without renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Simplified Second-Order Robust Double-Integral Sliding Mode Control of a Synchronous Cuk Converter Using a Modified Equivalent Control Law
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper describes a robust Proportional-Integral (PI)-based Double-Integral Sliding Mode Control (DI-SMC) technique for a Cuk converter. The DI-SMC technique is a dual-loop reduced simplified second-order control method, where only two state variables of the Cuk converter are controlled while retaining the desired control characteristics. An equivalent control law for the proposed control technique is derived by considering intersection of an invariant sliding manifold and its orthogonal manifold. Further, the controller parameters of the proposed control technique are tuned by considering a wide range of variations of the Cuk converter's system parameters and closed-loop stability analysis of the converter. The proposed technique includes a simplified robust on-line re-tuning of the feed-forward control loop gains instead of re-tuning the PI controller values, to enable ease of implementation and less modifications to the main control loop. The proposed control technique is verified using MATLAB/Simulink analysis under various test conditions.

articleTitle: Advanced Floating Point PID Controller For Cryo-Cooler Temperature Control in Infra-Red Payloads
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Infra-Red (IR) payloads are used on-board for measuring the thermal/spectral properties of objects. To reduce background and enhance Noise Equivalent Temperature Difference (NeTd), it is required to cool the detector (Focal Plane Assembly-FPA) and associated optics. Linear Sterling Cryo-Coolers are typically used for cooling of FPA. A diode temperature sensor is used to sense the cold tip (FPA) temperature. Long/Medium Wave Infra-Red sensors(LWIR/MIR) require tighter control of FPA temperature (Better than 15 mK (mili-Kelvin)). Since Diode sensor has a small output dynamic range of ∼500 mV (0.6 V to 1.1 V), therefore achieving stringent control is dependent on precise performance of design blocks (low noise current bias, high resolution temperature processing and PID Controller). Design of Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller plays a very crucial role in overall performance. Overshoot, settling time and stability are affected by PID design. Cooler Drive Electronics (CDE) is used to implement these functions. Truncation losses in a typical implementation of FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) based PID Controller leads to higher ripple. A Micro-controller based floating point PID controller is proposed to overcome these issues, thus enhancing the functionality to provide tighter control of Cooler temperature. In this paper we have discussed design and development of a Floating Point PID controller. A prototype (Enhanced CDE) was developed and tested in close loop with the peripheral sub-systems (Cryo-Cooler, Front End Camera Electronics(FECE), and Payload Power Supply(PPS» to demonstrate performance in actual payload environment. Short Term temperature stability of ~10mK RMS (Root Mean Square) and Long Term temperature stability of ~75mK (Peak to Peak) for Cryo-Cooler is achieved against the requirements of <15mK and <100mK respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Microgrid Resilience PlanningThrough Optimized Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In response to the imperative for resilient power distribution networks, we present a comprehensive approach to enhance the resiliency of an IEEE 123 bus distribution network through multi-objective optimization, primarily via demand response scheduling. Our framework focuses on minimizing cost and optimally reducing the load burden during islanded scenario. Objective functions encompass critical resiliency metrics, including reliability, restoration time, load shedding, and tie-switch adoption. We enforce constraints to ensure the network's practical feasibility, covering voltage limits, capacity restrictions, and operational considerations. NSGA II identifies Pareto-optimal solutions by assessing trade-offs between resiliency objectives, offering versatile strategies for bolstering network resiliency. These findings provide actionable insights for decision-makers, contributing to the fortification of distribution networks against disruptive events.

articleTitle: Power Losses Reduction in Distribution System Using PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research paper shows the minimization of power losses as well as to improve the voltage profile of the distribution system by using the reconfiguration of the network. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is used to identify the optimal location of the switch for reconfiguration of the network. Different cases of reconfiguration of the network are considered to study the proposed algorithm for 33-bus! and 69bus networks. The result shows that the solution is converged fastly and efficiently.

articleTitle: Different Power Quality Indices in The Electricity Services
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, different indices allied with power quality issues have been depicted by power distribution and utilization in the electricity services. Power quality issues are now the ground issue to conserve the electricity. Account of the harmonic indices and simple case study judge the reliability of the green power distribution and zero carbon emission as optimal solution of competitive green energy market

articleTitle: Li-Ion Battery State of Health Assessment Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The present and the upcoming world scenario is of battery applications such as Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS), Electric Vehicles (EVs), Renewable Energy Storage, Medical Devices, Aerospace and Satellites, Military Applications and many more. Majorly Li-ion battery is used in such applications. This paper proposes a methodology for battery health prediction using Machine Learning approach. Traditional approaches of Battery Health Management mostly focus on state of charge while the State of Health estimation is also very important for continuous operation. When determining a battery's State of Health (SOH), the deterioration of its rated capacity is commonly used, although determining a battery's capacity while it is operating is challenging task. Traditionally, laboratory measurements and offline analysis have been used extensively to determine the loss of rated capacity. In this work the definition of battery health status is given first. Then, feature extraction and model development is done. Finally, in this research, the performance of four regression models SVM, Regression Trees, Kernal Approximation Regression and Linear Regression Model are compared. The best regression model with Root Mean Square Error of 0.0152 is developed using the Linear Regression Model.

articleTitle: GAT- DNet: High Fidelity Graph Attention Network for Distribution Optimal Power Flow Pursuit
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The optimal operation of the distribution grid aims to efficiently manage the flow of electricity from sources to end-users, ensuring a resilient and sustainable grid. To perform optimal operation, Optimal Power Flow (OPF) plays a pivotal role in solving a complex optimization problem due to the system operational constraint and the provided OPF solutions. Traditional OPF algorithms are based on mathematical programming techniques, which can be computationally expensive and difficult to implement for complex large-scale networks. The most recent development in learning-based computational models has paradigm shifted towards data-driven approaches to OPF. This paper proposes a high-fidelity Graph Attention Networks (GAT) model that leverages the attention mechanism and graph convolution feature mapping to learn informative node representations for OPF solutions. We evaluated the proposed model on the IEEE-33 bus power distribution system, which is a representative example of a real-world distribution system. The proposed model outperformed the state-of-the-art MPGCN and DNN models in terms of loss function and performance evaluation indices. The proposed GAT model showcases its effectiveness and promises results for addressing the OPF problem in the distribution grid, as evidenced by performance evaluation metrics: MSE (0.0167), RMSE (0.1294), and MAE (0.0700), respectively.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Analysis of Energy Hub Integrated with Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: As the global energy landscape undergoes a transformative shift towards sustainability and resilience, the perception of energy hub has emerged as a promising solution. Energy hub is an integrated infrastructure that plays a pivotal role in generation, transmission and management of various forms of energy. This research paper presents a comprehensive techno economic analysis of energy hubs while considering different configurations to assess their feasibility and economic viability. The energy hub analyzed and examine the level of achievable operational flexibility and minimum cost with three types of load demand namely heat load, cooling or electricity load on time duration of 24 hours. The total cost has been reduced by using energy storage system, Combined heat power (CHP) and electric heat pump (EHP). The power delivered to three types of load demand represented by convergence characteristics.

articleTitle: Modified LMS/F Algorithm for Power Quality Improvement in Grid Connected PV system
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the execution analysis of threephase grid connected solar photovoltaic (SPV) using an improved LMS technique. The proposed work is based a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${L_p}$</tex> norm using Sparse Least mean square/fourth (LMS/F) control algorithm for the switching action of voltage source inverter (VSI) in synchronization with grid connected solar PV system. The efficiency of the system is shown in terms of harmonic reduction. Results also show a seamless transition during unbalancing conditions of the system operation. Simulation of the proposed model is efficiently carried on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Boost Converter Based PLL for Single Phase Grid Connected Solar PV
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a comparative analysis of different Phase Locked Loop's (PLL's) for single-phase systems with Solar PV integration circuit in order to track accurate phase angle and frequency. Four models such as: conventional PLL, SRFPLL, EPLL, SOGI based PLL have been proposed. Firstly, mathematical modelling using transfer function is designed to analyze the stability with the help of bode plot. Secondly, performance of all models have been analysed on the basis of settling time and damping factor to reduce the transients overshoot at the time of synchronization. Two cases have been proposed in the first case the system is tested under voltage imbalance and in the second case the system is tested under frequency jump. The results under both cases clearly indicated that the SOGI based PLL outperformed with minimum value of damping factor (K) 1.20. The simulations are conducted in MATLAB/Simulink for the verification of results.

articleTitle: A Novel Power Flow Control Scheme of Grid-Battery Integrated Induction Motor Driven E-Mobility Charger
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research paper presents an efficient strategy for managing power in electric vehicle batteries to enhance their interaction with the electric grid. This approach not only enables battery charging through the grid but in similar manner it allows for supplying electricity towards the grid when needed. The electric vehicle employs sensorless field-oriented control (FOC) of an induction motor, driven by a Voltage Source Converter (VSC) at grid side and a Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) for motor control. Two way power flow is achieved with the help of a bidirectional buck-boost converter. To regulate the two way power flow between the 3-phase VSI and the common DC bus voltage that connects to the electric vehicle's induction motor drive, the Unit Vector Template (UVT) concept is utilized. Additionally, this system improves power quality by reducing total harmonic distortion (THD) and maintaining a unity power factor (UPF). The paper outlines the mathematical model and the power management approach for the entire system, and it presents and analyses the results obtained from simulations conducted in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Bridgeless Hybrid Converter Fed Switched Reluctance Motor For Household Appliances
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: A non-isolated hybrid bridgeless (NHB) converter is designed for power quality management in switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive. A low cost SRM motor drive is selected for household appliances and is fed through NHB converter for efficient motor control. This converter is operated in discontinuous current mode (DCM). A mid-point is developed using zeta and canonical switching cell (CSC) converter. NHB converter is developed to compensate for grid voltage variations ranging from 90V to 270V. Split capacitor voltages are regulated for speed control of SRM drive. NHB converter components are selected to perform satisfactorily for 600 W power rating. This study presents an analysis, design, and simulation of a low-cost SRM drive with a front-end converter aimed at household appliances.

articleTitle: Structural Analysis and Determination of Critical Speed of a 10,000 rpm Switched Reluctance Machine Rotor
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: High-speed machines are gaining popularity in the modern age due to their high power density. While they offer advantages, they also pose several electrical and mechanical challenges. In a particular high-speed application like turbo-machines, the rotor is subjected to the high temperature of order 500°C or above. In such operating conditions, switched reluctance machines with solid rotor are viable solutions as it does not contain any winding and permanent magnets on its rotor. The mechanical characteristics of the rotor, such as stress, deformations, natural frequencies, and critical speeds, need to be found for a given rotor design to ensure the safe and reliable operation. This paper presents an analysis of solid rotors used in 10,000 rpm Switched reluctance machines (SRM) using the finite element analysis (FEA) tool, ANSYS. The FEA analysis determines the maximum stress and deformation of rotor at various loads and speeds. The natural frequencies and mode shapes of the rotor are determined under free-free condition. Further, the critical speed of the rotor are estimated considering the effect of the bearing stiffness and rotor speed on the natural frequencies. This study confirms the rigid rotor operation at 10,000 rpm with a separation margin of 33% from the critical speed (i.e., 15,000 rpm).

articleTitle: Improved Low Frequency Oscillation Damping of an AC Microgrid With Sophisticated Filter-Based Power Oscillation Damping Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research paper aims to improve the oscillation damping with the influence of measurement or Gaussian noise in AC microgrid systems. The idea of designing an analog filter network is used as the lead-lag-based power oscillations damping (POD) controllers to enhance the damping performance with or without the imperfect communication medium used in the test system. The lead-lag POD controller was unable to deal with the noise and delay signal and the system performance became unstable. The robust design of a filter-based POD controller deals with the constraint of an imperfect communication medium, that includes measurement noise, process noise, and delay in signal in the system. The optimal control signal and controller placement are chosen using the residue approach. The lead-lag damping controller's source of employment is to dampen low-frequency oscillations in the system, but if the system consideration with an imperfect communication medium, then the filter-based POD controller improves the damping performance with the uncertainties in disturbance of the test system. The Gaussian random noise is used to model an imperfect communication medium-based network. Employing MATLAB/SIMULINK software to simulate an AC microgrid test system, the performance of Butterworth low pass filter-based PODC and lead-lad PODC are compared. The outcomes of simulations illustrate the performance of the Butterworth low pass filter-based POD controller is more efficient under an imperfect communication medium such as noise with fault conditions.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Online Prognosis of State of Charge of Lithium-Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have become an important part of energy storage systems. The prognosis of the parameters is important for the battery management system which effectively increases the life of the battery and protects it from fault. This study concentrates on the accurate state of charge (SoC) of Lithium-ion Batteries using the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and Particle Filter (PF) methods. The EKF is a signal-tracking algorithm but PF is a likelihood algorithm based on Bayesian probability theory. In this study, a forgetting factor recursive least square (FF-RLS) algorithm is used to estimate 1RC battery model parameters. The (FF-RLS) algorithm is embedded with the EKF filter for the prognosis of the SoC of the lithium-ion battery using terminal Voltage and Current Signals. The PF outperforms the EKF in terms of the accuracy of the SoC estimation of the battery.

articleTitle: A Reactive Power Controller for a Two-Stage Transformerless PV Grid System by Employing Virtual Inertia Control
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The rising integration of photovoltaic (PV) energy with the grid has several impacts on electrical power systems which demands a properly designed control scheme to maintain the power balance along with the voltage stability at the grid integration point commonly known as the Point of Common Coupling (PCC). As the PV systems are non-inertial and produce only active power, hence without regulating the reactive power the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PV$</tex> microgrids often cause reactive power disturbances as well as transmission line impedance errors to the grids. Thus, while penetrating with grids, maintaining active and reactive powers simultaneously with the proper controlling of voltage and frequency of the PV systems is a challenging task. In this work, a virtual inertia control scheme is proposed for a two-stage transformerless PV grid system to maintain both active and reactive power of the system while changing system voltage under variable irradiance conditions. The control scheme is virtual and based on the dynamic equations involved with the synchronous generator. The overall system is simulated under MATLAB/SIMULINK and results are presented showing the control parameter performances including the DC bus voltage, grid voltage, frequency, active power, and reactive power. The results show that with the variation of system voltage, the control scheme is capable of maintaining the active and reactive power by varying the frequency along with the grid and inverter voltage and current.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Study of Optical Float-Zone Grown Gallium Oxide Schottky Barrier Diode
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> based lateral Schottky barrier diodes are fabricated using Ni/Au as Schottky contact and Ti/Au as Ohmic contact. The Sn-doped β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> sample is grown by the optical float-zone technique. The effect of trenches, which are used for mesa isolation, on break-down voltage is investigated. The device shows near-ideal characteristics in terms of built-in potential. The parasitic series and shunt resistance are extracted, and their dependency on temperature is established. Comprehensive modeling of temperature-dependent reverse leakage current is demonstrated using the thermionic emission (TE) model, Poole-Frenkel (PF) emission model, and Fowler-Nordheim (FN) tun-neling mechanism. The procedure to extract relevant parameters is explained in terms of bias and temperature dependency. The combined model shows excellent agreement with experimental data over a wide range of bias and temperature. The maximum electric field of 2.3 MV/cm is achieved.
