articleTitle: Analysis of Power Modulations in Resonant Dual Active Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of power modulations in the Resonant Dual Active Bridge (RDAB) DC-DC converter, considering different pulse-widthmodulation techniques. A comparison is made between the extended-phase-shift (EPS) and dual-phase-shift (DPS) power modulation techniques in the RDAB DCDC converter. The objective is to achieve high power transfer efficiency throughout the entire range of operation. To accomplish this, a hybrid power modulation technique merging EPS and DPS techniques is proposed. The validation of the proposed scheme is conducted through MATLAB/SIMULINK software to assess its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 3-Phase Active Front End PWM Rectifier for Air-Core Two-Coil WPT System Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Wireless battery charging has emerged as a promising technology for electric vehicles (EVs), eliminating the need for physical connections. This study presents a wireless battery charger designed specifically for EV charging applications. The charger utilizes the AC grid's electricity for power factor correction during wireless charging. The charging process comprises four stages: AC-DC conversion, DC-HFAC inversion, wireless power transfer (WPT), and HFAC-DC rectification. An Active Front Rectifier, controlled using the three-phase synchronous reference frame theory (SRFT), ensures a stable DC voltage for efficient charging. The suggested charger implements a WPT scheme, enabling charging without a local controller at the vehicle end. This approach offers convenience, improved energy transfer, and potential integration into existing charging infrastructure. The findings contribute to the advancement of wireless battery charging technology, enhancing the sustainability and convenience of EVs.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Interleaved ZETA Converter used for EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this paper, an electrical vehicle battery charger based on interleaved ZETA converter is analyzed with performance parameters. In recent era, Electrical Vehicles are better alternative to internal combustion (ICE) based vehicles and electrical vehicles (EVs) are greener mode of transport for people. So there is increase in use of Electrical Vehicle (EV) as per global demand. The need of battery charger for electrical vehicle in either case on-board or off-board is essential. The electrical vehicle charger produces certain impact on utility system from where it is supplied energy. In this study, the Interleaved ZETA converter is used which supplies the required DC voltage as L1 level charger to the Electrical Vehicle Battery. The ZETA converter has low ripple content and non-inversion voltage at output side. The proposed topology of interleaved converter is analyzed with performance parameters through simulation carried out in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Impact of Electric Vehicle on Distribution System: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are playing a vital role in overcoming the problem of fuel price hiking. Nowadays customers are taking a keen interest in EVs due to a lot of benefits. As the number of EVs increases the load demand for charging also increases which generates stress on the distribution system. This paper provides a detailed review of the Impact of EV charging on the distribution system. Different power quality problems are introduced due to the charging and discharging of EV batteries.

articleTitle: Parallel Distributed Energy Generation Based Microgrid Incorporating Reactive Power Sharing and Grid Synchronisation Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents multiple parallel distributed energy sources (DERs) based generating unit connected to a common <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AC$</tex> bus for supplying uninterrupted power to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AC$</tex> local loads while exercising on power quality of microgrid (MG). Main focus of this work is a) to share net reactive power demand of loads between parallel voltage source converters (which minimize burden of single converter) and 2) has capability to synchronize to the grid, when the grid is available (seamless grid synchronization ability). Sliding Goertzel pre-filter-based frequency locked loop is used to calculate fundamental component of local loads and also to obtain frequency during grid synchronization also when the grid is subjected to voltages unbalance. A brushless direct current (BLDC) machine is used as a wind generating unit because it is independent of voltage and frequency fluctuations at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{AC}$</tex> bus unlike other conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{AC}$</tex> generators. Wind energy conversion and solar energy conversion system along with a battery storage are connected to form a MG, which is modelled and its performance is simulated in MATLAB and adaptability of MG is found through obtained results.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fault Classification in Hybrid Microgrid Using Different Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The reliability of the power system is impacted by protection challenges in microgrids due to the increased integration of distributed generators that supply local loads. To enhance overall power system resilience, addressing these challenges is crucial. Conventional protection systems face challenges in reliably identifying bidirectional power flow during power exchanges between microgrids and the main grid. Adaptive intelligent protection methods offer a solution, adapting to grid changes, operational modes, and energy resource variations. This study conducted a comparative analysis of implementing different machine learning algorithms, such as Artificial Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks, and k-Nearest Neighbors, for fault classification in a hybrid microgrid in standalone mode. The input dataset comprises three-phase currents and voltages, aimed at accurately identifying 11 fault types and instances without faults. Microgrid simulations are conducted in MATLAB/Simulink, while Python software is used for testing and training. This research assesses the effectiveness of these algorithms in improving fault classification within microgrids using accuracy as the primary parameter. The findings indicate that Convolutional Neural Networks outperform Artificial Neural Networks and k-Nearest Neighbors in this study.

articleTitle: Mitigating Congestion Problems Using GR and 20 MW Wind Turbine Utilizing JAYA Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The power system is grappling with congestion issues due to technological advancements and deregulation, leading to fierce competition among private generators and a lack of transparency in transactions. To ensure a reliable and efficient power system, alleviating congestion is crucial for the system. Among various mitigation strategies, generator rescheduling is a key method, though it raises generation costs, and this cost can be reduced by selecting generators based on sensitivity factors utilizing an optimization algorithm to determine optimal power rescheduling. In addition, the congestion costs can be significantly reduced by allowing wind power penetration and thus reducing the number of generators involved in rescheduling. This paper explores the impact of wind power integration on congestion costs in the conventional energy system. It introduces a novel approach using bus sensitivity factors for precise wind turbine placement and combines it with the JAYA Optimization algorithm. The results, validated on the IEEE modified 30 Bus system, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed over other algorithms in the literature, leading to substantial congestion cost reductions.

articleTitle: Re-Evaluation of the Conventional and AI-Based MPPT Techniques in PVPG Systems in Indian Scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) energy has made significant remarks in meeting global electrical energy needs in recent years. The solar photovoltaic array, which is created by interconnecting several solar cells in parallel and series, is used by photovoltaic (PV) systems to generate electricity. A controller is required to achieve this, as the solar panel cannot be forced to run at its extreme power point by the photovoltaic (PV) system. Along with the well-optimized controller, the system will have the desired output, and settling time can also be reduced. Therefore, to produce more energy from the sun and fulfill the global need for electrical energy from the photovoltaic system, maximum power point (MPP) trackers along with a solar array are required. This paper provides a re-evaluation of different conventional and AI-based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques for photovoltaic arrays. The most commonly used MPP tracker methods are modeled and reviewed. The modeled MPP trackers are evaluated in the same environmental conditions with the same photovoltaic system. MATLAB Simulink is used to model and simulate the system. The benefits and drawbacks of each MPP tracking approach are highlighted in the final section.

articleTitle: Interleaved Boost Converter Based Solar PV Plant for Distributed Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a substantial increase in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) due to growing concerns about carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions, attempt to reduce dependency on fossil fuels, and a push towards renewable energy sources. To support the expanding adoption of electric vehicles, it is necessary to grow the EV battery charging stations. This paper presents an approach for charging of Lithium-ion batteries used in the EVs directly from solar energy through photovoltaic (PV) systems for distributed charging stations. For optimal performance, the PV system is operated at its maximum power point (MPP). In scenarios where EV battery charging is distributed across a larger area, a higher-rated solar PV plant is considered. To improve power handling and to minimize input current fluctuations, an interleaved boost DC-DC converter (IBC) is employed. Charging of the multiple EV batteries is facilitated using the distributed phase-shift full bridge converters. The battery charging process follows the constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) technique to align with the Li-ion battery's charging requirements. The proposed approach for distributed EV battery charging is implemented using the MATLAB/Simulink software tool for verification of results.

articleTitle: A New Dual-Adaptive Inertia Strategy Controller Based UPQC to Improve the Power Quality of Hybrid Renewable Energy System Connected to Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The increasing concern for energy security has raised global awareness of renewable energy resources. Wind and solar energy systems, significant contributors to renewable, play a vital role in addressing climate change, reducing energy costs, improving power supply reliability, and increasing energy accessibility. With power quality becoming a growing concern for utility companies, engineers face the challenge of maintaining power quality due to variable operating characteristics and reliance on weather conditions. Additionally, advancements in power electronic devices for controlling nonlinear loads have impacted power quality in the electrical distribution grid. Therefore, it is crucial to prioritize the quality of power delivered to loads. The Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) emerges as a promising solution to address power quality issues. This paper introduces a new Dual Adaptive Inertia Strategy Controller-based UPQC to enhance the power quality of hybrid renewable energy systems, incorporating Squirrel Cage Induction Generator-based Wind Energy Systems and Solar PV systems connected to the grid. The performance of this proposed UPQC controller is compared to controllers based on Virtual Synchronous Machine and Instantaneous Power theory using MATLAB SIMULINK. The results demonstrate that the proposed UPQC controller effectively enhances power quality for hybrid renewable systems under various power quality conditions, in accordance with IEEE standards.

articleTitle: Single-Stage, Improved Power Quality Converter for Electric Vehicle Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents a single-stage, improved power quality, on-board charger based on isolated cuk converter topology for battery charging in electric vehicle (EV) applications. To obtain sinusoidal current at the utility side, a voltage follower control strategy is opted for. The converter is designed such that it operates in real inductive discontinuous conduction mode which results into unity power factor operation. Lead acid battery is charged using this converter topology in constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) modes respectively. A 0.76 kW, CC-CV charger with a maximum current rating of 11.7A is developed to charge a 100Ah e-bike battery. Performance of such a charger is simulated in MATLAB environment in discrete time frame. Controller is able to overcome any variations in supply at rated load conditions. At 20kHz switching frequency, operation of the converter shows harmonics-free input current for the presented circuit which is in coherence with IEC 61000-3-2.

articleTitle: A Real- Time Prognosis of State of Charge and State of Health of Remote Lithium-ion Battery on IoT Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: this study concentrates on realtime estimation of state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH) on cloud platforms. The cloud offers the storage vast storage and computational facilities that can be utilized for realtime applications. Initially, a hardware loop is used to obtain the experimental data set to find the initial parameter of the I-RC model and form a regression model of the battery. A joint estimator is used for SoC and SoH estimation at different time scales. SoC is the critical parameter for a battery management system (BMS). Therefore it must be estimated at a shorter duration of micro intervals. SoH of the battery is calculated at the end of each life cycle of the battery. A strong calibration of time scaling is done while computing SoC and SoH at different durations of time. The forgetting factor recursive least square (FFRLS) method estimated the battery model parameters which is used by the extended Kalman filter EKF for SoC estimation at micro time scale. The important realtime estimation of SoC and SoH are stored in DBMS and they can be shown on the user interface graphically with the help of API (application programming interface).

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Li-ion Battery based on Equivalent Circuit Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Most modern technology, including Electric Vehicles (EVs) & energy storage device are powered by Lithium ion Batteries (LiB). The advantages of this kind of battery over other battery types include greater energy density & reliability. They must be managed using a battery management system (BMS), which ensures their safety and improves their performance under normal circumstances, for them to function properly. Accurate estimation of the State of Charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) is very critical in EVs. The lithium-ion battery is a highly time-invariant, nonlinear, and complicated electrochemical system, making this task extremely difficult. In this article, we provide a cell model that may be applied to the process of estimating the charge. This model relies on an electrical approach known as the Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM), in which we construct an electrical circuit with the same behavior as the actual cell. We will use cuttingedge methodologies to establish the model parameters using a set of laboratory data. The estimation of the SOC, SOH and other internal parameters will use these variables.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Customizable Neural Network Models for Solar Irradiance Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The solar irradiance is one of the key parameters used for the generation of electrical power from solar energy. This study discusses about one of the scopes of improving the solar irradiance forecasting models. The solar irradiance forecasting models presented in the study has been analyzed for two types of feature engineering techniques, i.e., PCA (Principal Component Analysis) and kPCA (kernel Principal Component Analysis). Simultaneously, the feature engineered dataset has been trained with different activation functions and different combinations of hidden layer neurons-based Cas-NN (Cascaded Neural Network) forecasting models. The training of different test models suggests that the original dataset engineered with kPCA and combined with Tan sigmoid activation function including higher hidden layer neurons is performing better than other considered test models.

articleTitle: A Novel Beluga Whale Optimization and Loss Sensitivity Factor Method for Optimal Capacitors Placement in Radial Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this study, a novel optimization algorithm, namely the Beluga Whale Optimization Algorithm (BWO) with Loss sensitivity factor (LSF) is employed to determine the optimal locations and sizes of capacitors in radial distribution system. The objective is to enhance the voltage profile and curtail active power losses by strategically placing capacitors at suitable locations and determining their optimal sizes. Through extensive simulations, the performance of BWO is evaluated and contrasted with other conventional metaheuristic methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of all algorithms in enhancing the voltage profile and reducing power losses. Nonetheless, BWO demonstrates faster convergence and higher solution quality in comparison. The algorithm intelligently explores the solution space, adapting the concepts of bubble-net feeding and echolocation employed by beluga whales. This enables BWO to converge efficiently towards the global optimum, outperforming other optimization methods in most scenarios. We have opted to utilize two IEEE test bus systems, namely IEEE 33 and IEEE 69, to implement the suggested technique. These systems have been specifically designed to closely replicate real-world distribution network scenarios, thus ensuring accurate testing and evaluation.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Heffron-Phillips SMIB Model with Integrated Power System Stabilizer and Effect of Time Delay
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The Heffron-Phillips Single Machine Infinite Bus (SMIB) model, integrated with a power system stabilizer (PSS), offers a comprehensive depiction of a synchronous generator linked to an infinite bus within a power network. This model adeptly captures the interplay of mechanical and electrical aspects of the generator, along with the impact of a power system stabilizer on overall stability. The PSS acts as a control mechanism to attenuate oscillations and enhance dynamic stability. The synchronous generator's traits, including inertia, damping, and electrical characteristics, are represented in the Heffron-Phillips SMIB model. The turbine governor and excitation systems symbolize the mechanical and electrical components, respectively. These elements interact internally and with the external power system through voltage and mechanical power. Incorporating time delay in the power system stabilizer adds complexity, stemming from communication and processing delays. Modeling a delayed PSS within the Heffron-Phillips framework demands scrutiny of its impact on system dynamics. Time delays can influence control system stability and performance, necessitating careful analysis and tuning.

articleTitle: A Combined Simulink Model of Hybrid System Using SMES, TCSC Tuned Using Cuckoo Search
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In this electronic document the study of a two-area hybrid energy system is considered for load frequency control under the deregulated environment. The hybrid energy system consists of thermal-hydro-nuclear-diesel and gas power plants. This system is designed to overcome the limitations of individual energy sources while leveraging their respective advantages, resulting in improved efficiency, reliability, and sustainability. To compensate for reactive power AVR is connected to the system to regulate and stabilize the output voltage of a generator. A high-speed energy exchange device, SMES is used when a surplus of power or shortage of power takes place. The TCSC is used to improve the stability of the system. To overcome deviation in frequency, tie-line power and voltage PID tuner is used to reduce settling time up to 12.5 second. To obtain the optimum gain of PID, TCSC, and SMES the novel- Cuckoo Search optimization technique is implemented. The whole interconnected hybrid system is designed on MATLAB Simulink-2016b.

Author Keywords: Super Magnetic Energy Storage Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor

articleTitle: Implementation of Lyapunov Function-Based Hybrid Controller in Semi-Quadratic Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This article presents a novel Semi-Quadratic buckboost converter (SQBuBoC) designed to integrate in many applications with a wide range of output voltage such as photovoltaic systems. The efficient control and energy management of renewable-driven stand-alone systems has been areas of active research. However, effectively managing both the renewable energy source and the distributed energy stored while meeting the load requirements remains a challenge. This study focuses on evaluating the performance of a SQBuBoC with a Lyapunov function-based controller. The proposed controller employs a combination of a duty-ratio feedforward control unit and a Lyapunov function-based control unit. The duty-ratio feedforward control unit is responsible for reducing the workload on the feedback controller. By utilizing this control scheme, the closedloop system achieves exponential stability and exhibits excellent transient responsiveness, even when subjected to significant disturbance. The MATLAB simulation outcomes are showcased to demonstrate and exemplify the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Resonant Estimator Assisted Closed Loop Observer for Speed Sensor-Less Control of Syn-Rel Motor for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: An optimization of sensor count is a crucial aspect in implementation of synchronous reluctance (Syn-Rel) motor drive in electric vehicle (EV) propulsion system. This contributes to enhancing dependability and stability of system. However, achieving seamless operation of sensorless control over a complete driving range of speed remains a substantial challenge. This paper presents an adaptive resonant estimator (ARE) assisted sliding mode observer (SMO) with improved EMFs for wide range of speed control and drive speed and position are estimated with enhanced quadrature phase locked loop (e-QPLL) technique. In contrast to other methods, presented technique improves back EMF for complete driving range with minimal speed and position error. An augmentation in drive response to varying load demand is observed for all vehicle speed as a result of improved speed and position estimations. Analysis and validation of presented system are done in a comprehensive manner in MATLAB/Simulink. A detailed illustration of vehicle's dynamics and motor-driving capacity are also provided here.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Type-II and Type-III Controllers for Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Power Electronic DC/DC buck converters are being extensively employed in power supply applications such as mobile phones, computers, communication setups and many more. These power electronic converters are normally operated in closed-loop configuration in order to attain precise control over the desired output. Buck converters in closed loop are generally stable but do not provide decent performance, therefore, a controller in the loop is necessary to tune the performance parameters to appropriate specifications. This paper discusses different types of controllers have been designed and analyzed for desired stability margins for a DC/DC buck converter in frequency domain. MATLAB/Simulink software has been utilized for the analysis and design of these controllers.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Power Transfer in Wireless Power Transfer Applications using Active Power Source
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Wireless charging technique has widespread usage in modern world. Its applications include electronic gadget and Electric Vehicle (EVs) charging. This paper presents the technique to enhance power transfer capabilities in wireless power transfer applications. The wireless power system consists of a DC supply, full bridge converter, mutual inductor, full-bridge rectifier and a charging load. The paper presents a configuration in which an active power source is introduced on the receiver side of the wireless power transfer system. The paper firstly considers an injection of ideal AC source in quadrature with the transmitted current for enhancement of real power transfer. The quadrature injection ensures net zero real power exchange with the active source. The analogy has been drawn from the concept of static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) used for power enhancement in power transmission lines. Next an injection inverter is used with LC Filter for verification of the power enhancement. The input and output power increases by increasing the injected AC voltage. Results are verified through the MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation model. A high sampling frequency simulation is used for realizing high pulse frequency of 50 kHz in main inverter and switching frequency of 500 kHz for active injection inverter.

articleTitle: Incremental Conductance-Based MPPT for Photovoltaic Systems Utilizing PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: To achieve the high-power output from solar arrays, it is crucial for the PV system to operate at the maximum power point (MPP). Determination of MPP is essential for the effective operation of solar arrays. The present paper showcases the incremental conductance (INC) approach to track the MPP for PV system under variable environmental circumstances. The PI controller has been used to extract maximum power and the analysis shows the increase in efficiency under different variables like temperature, irradiance, and load. The results have been obtained using MATLAB Simulink model.

articleTitle: Voltage and Frequency Control of Distributed Generation Using Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Voltage and frequency control of a distributed generation (DG) is a challenge unless it is associated with a synchronous generator. The is because the system lacks inherit inertia because of involvement of converter as an interlinking device between DG and load. A battery energy storage system (BESS) may be utilized to attain the power balance during various switching and power imbalance conditions. This paper presents a DG set with frequency and voltage control utilizing a BESS. Various switching scenarios and power imbalance conditions are created to see the performance of test system. The simulation is done in MATLAB and the test system works well during various switching and power imbalance scenarios. Computer simulations are done in MATLAB.

Author Keywords: battery energy storage system and voltage source inverter

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Energy Integration and Fossil Fuel Reduction in a Hybrid PV, Battery, Grid, and Diesel System: A Robust Energy Management Algorithm Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research study introduces an advanced Energy Management Algorithm (EMA) that aims to improve the efficiency, sustainability, and robustness of a Hybrid PV, Battery, Grid, and Diesel energy system. The suggested Energy Management Algorithm (EMA) aims to tackle the crucial issue of efficiently and effectively balancing different energy resources in light of the rising integration of renewable energy sources and the escalating need for reliable power supply. The method incorporates considerations for the intermittent characteristics of solar photovoltaic (PV) generation, the energy storage capacity of batteries, the grid as a contingency power source, and the dependability of diesel generators in offgrid situations. Through the strategic scheduling of these components, the EMA effectively enhances energy efficiency, mitigates operational expenses, and diminishes the release of greenhouse gas emissions. The system demonstrates the capacity to adjust to varying environmental circumstances, load profiles, and grid availability, therefore guaranteeing an uninterrupted and sustainable energy provision. Moreover, it places a high priority on utilizing renewable sources in order to mitigate environmental consequences. By conducting comprehensive simulations, the suggested Energy Management Algorithm (EMA) exhibits notable advancements in system efficiency, economic feasibility, and environmental sustainability. This study makes a significant academic contribution to the field of energy management by proposing a helpful solution for hybrid energy systems. Furthermore, it advocates for the dependable and robust integration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Adaptive Non-Linear Observer Based Current-Sensorless Operation of Series-Stacked Buffer
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Single-phase grid connected converters have an issue of power mismatch, which can be rectified by an active or passive energy storage element. Among active storage energy storage solution, series-stacked buffer (SSB) has emerged as a desirable choice due to its improved power density and high energy utilization capability. However, SSB exhibits the high-sensor requirement when compared to other state-of-the-art active storage energy storage solutions. To achieve improved performance and current-sensorless control, this paper presented an adaptive nonlinear current observer (ANCO) based control for SSB. Without using any differential functions, ANCO based control technique for SSB control is also able to provide disturbance rejection caused by parameter mismatch. Moreover, due ANCO's noise filtering capability, reliable performance of SSB is facilitated. The proof-of-concept of presented ANCO based control method is verified by simulation, by applying it to SSB connected to a typical AC-DC converter rated at 1kW.

articleTitle: Fast Transient Recovery of Common DC Bus Architecture with Large Signal Based Tuning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The generic architecture of a common DC bus configuration is designed using multiple interconnected power converters connected in cascaded/parallel fashion. A rigidly controlled power consuming converter (PCC) behaves as constant power type load (CPL) across common bus. Moreover, a load transient across PCC results as power transient for power delivering converters (PDCs). Due to interconnected system configuration, coupling effect emerges during small signal based (SSB) controller tuning process. In order to fulfill margin requirements, the controller may need to be tuned repeatedly. Moreover, tuned parameters may not result in fast transient performance considering wider operating range. To achieve faster transient recovery, the large signal based (LSB) tuning approach with peak current mode control followed by output current feed-forward logic is adopted in this work for the droop controlled PDCs. The effect of droop term is considered during the derivation of proportional gain magnitude for load step up transients in PCCs. Implementation procedure along with simulation case studies is presented considering different load step up transient cases for the overall interconnected convert system. This control approach helps to acquire fast transient response without disturbing operation of other PCC in the system.

articleTitle: Analysing the Design and Performance of a Controller for AGC in Multi-Source Systems Using Cuckoo Search Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system is pivotal for ensuring power system stability and reliability by aligning generator power output with load demand and maintaining a precise system frequency. Conventional AGC, employing a PID controller within a secondary automatic load frequency controller (SALFC), encounters issues like settling time, rise time, and power output overshoots. This paper proposes a remedy using the cuckoo search optimization technique to fine-tune AGC's PID parameters and mitigate these limitations. The study applies the cuckoo search algorithm to a two-area multi-source power system, incorporating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and Non-Renewable sources in a restructured interconnected network, including photovoltaic and grid-integrated wind turbines. Performance evaluation centers on minimizing ISE, ITSE, IAE, and ITAE. The system encompasses Thermal with reheat turbines, hydroelectric, Gas-based, solar, and Wind power stations. Comparing results with PID tuning through GA and GWO, the simulations demonstrate the superiority of the cuckoo search-based AGC, offering a promising avenue for smarter and more effective AGC systems in enhancing power grid stability and reliability.

articleTitle: Operation Strategies and Energy Market Structure for Hybrid Microgrid Using Intelligent Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Hybrid microgrids are a promising solution to meet the challenges of modern energy systems. By combining multiple energy sources with energy storage and control technologies, hybrid microgrids provide reliable, affordable, and sustainable power to communities, businesses, and homes. They can operate in both grid-tied and stand-alone modes, providing resilience and flexibility to the power grid. Hybrid microgrids have attracted significant attention from researchers, policymakers and industry stakeholders worldwide due to their potential to transform the traditional power grid into a more resilient, decentralized and sustainable system. The impact of hybrid microgrids on the energy market and the environment will depend on various factors, such as the cost of the technology and the regulatory framework. It is important to carefully consider these factors to ensure that the development of hybrid microgrids leads to a more sustainable and equitable energy future. This research introduces a novel algorithm aimed at minimizing the operating costs of a microgrid over a 24-hour time horizon. The algorithm achieves this by optimizing the power allocation of DGs (Distributed Generators) while accounting for the inherent randomness associated with DGs, both in the presence and absence of Grid. To achieve this goal, hybrid optimization technique involves the utilization of Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (APSO) Algorithm to optimize the main objective function based on Net Present Value (NPV) method, and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm to optimize the Energy Management System (EMS) strategy cost in microgrids. The APSO algorithm optimizes the capacity of Distributed Generation (DG) units and batteries, while the EMS strategy cost is optimized based on quadratic programming by considering the constraints. These methods collectively enable the microgrid to efficiently manage its energy resources while also determining the appropriate operational strategies.

articleTitle: High Gain Quadratic Boost-Cuk Converter Based on Switched Capacitor for Fuel Cell Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Due to limited resources and global warming conditions, there is a paradigm shift in transportation from petrochemical to electric vehicles. Fuel cell vehicles are the emerging source of electric vehicles. Still, a wide range of voltage gain is required for the Fuel cell electric vehicles, which are satisfied by high-gain DC-DC converters to sustain the DC-link voltage from low-voltage fuel cell stacks. This study proposed a non-isolated DC-DC converter suitable for such applications to provide high gain for fuel cell electric vehicles. The proposed converters offer large step-up voltage by utilizing a single ground-referenced active power switch by combining the key features of switched capacitors, quadratic Boost, and Cuk converters. Compared to a conventional boost converter, the proposed converter reduces the voltage stress across the active power switch and can be used for high-power applications. The proposed converter is designed and driven, and its simulations are proofread and verified in MATLAB atmosphere.

articleTitle: Accurate Motor Current Sensing for Fine Torque Control of Actuators in Robotic Arms
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Accurate measurement of motor current is essential for fine current control and in turn torque control of actuators. The paper presents a current sensing scheme suited for motion control of robotic actuators driven by a three-phase BLDC motor. A low-side current sensing scheme with a triple current sensor is employed to acquire the motor current rather than the commonly used methods with the single current sensor. The method demonstrated in this paper provides accurate measurement of motor current with minimum hardware resources. Various practical aspects affecting the current measurements are discussed. The efficacy of the scheme is evaluated by acquiring motor current data using a microcontroller and comparing it against the actual current flowing through the motor.

articleTitle: Development of Solar-powered EV Charging Station With Energy Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper explains design and development of solar based electric vehicle (EV) charging station (EVCS) using the reachability concept sliding mode controller (RCSMC). The proposed system is modular and environmentally friendly. The system optimization is accomplished by an energy management system (EMS). It is required to utilize solar PV power as much as possible. The EMS strategy of SPEV system is designed in such a way that the EV is charged efficiently either by the PV or by the distribution grid. An improved EMS is designed for automatically manage the power distribution for charging the EV battery, supply to load of home appliances and rest to grid. The availability of power in different modes of operations, such as PV-EV, PV-Grid, Grid- EV and EVGrid and for smooth conduction, the proposed system employs several power electronics converters. The DC-DC boost converter with incremental conductance (INC) based maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controller and DC-DC bidirectional converter with RCSMC controller for battery charging and discharging. An improved energy management system (EMS) is designed for automatically manage the power distribution for charging the EV battery, supply to load of home appliances and rest to grid. It is verified through the result of MATLAB/Simulink.

Author Keywords: bidirectional buck-boost converter with RCSMC based controller

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Classification of Defects in Pcb Using Deep Learning Techniques: A Comparison of Resnet50v1 and Efficient Det D1
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: To keep pace with the fast-growing Printed Circuit Board (PCB) industry, automated processes are necessary for producing flawless products. Automated visual PCB inspections have become indispensable for addressing the challenges posed by conventional manual inspection systems, as they offer faster, more quantitative, and objective assessments. The aim of this research is to determine an appropriate and effective Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithm for detecting and classifying different PCB defects. Two CNN algorithms, namely Single Shot Detector-Residual Neural Network 50 V1 Model (SSD ResNet50v1) and Efficient Object Detector Model D1 (EfficientDet D1), are evaluated for their classification performance, and their results are compared. The training of these models is conducted on Google Colaboratory, a cloud-based service that provides a free online Jupyter notebook environment for deep learning model training on NVIDIA's Graphical Processing Unit (GPU). The PCB dataset comprises 10,668 images of size 600 × 600 with six common PCB defects frequently found in the industry. The study calculates the classification performance of both algorithms and presents their results. The accuracy achieved by SSD ResNet50v1 is 81.68%, while EfficientDet D1 reaches 71.75%. A comparison of both architectures' accuracies shows that SSD ResNet50v1 performs better than EfficientDet D1.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Optimization of a Parasitic Buck Converter Using Leverrier's Algorithm and PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This paper presents the modelling of a second-order DC-DC converter using the State Space Averaging (SSA) technique in the presence of non-idealities of active and passive components, especially source resistance, which researchers ignore. The resolvent matrix of the linearised state-space model needs to be calculated to acquire the small signal transfer function of a DC-DC buck converter. Therefore, this paper introduces a simple systematic approach to obtain the resolvent matrix. This approach is derived from Leverrier's Algorithm. The conventional matrix inversion formula for acquiring a resolvent matrix is cumbersome, whereas this method is quite efficient. To demonstrate the implementation of this algorithm, duty cycle-to-output voltage and input voltage-to-output voltage transfer functions of second-order buck converter are acquired. A PI controller is also implemented in the DC-DC converter to synchronize its output voltage with input voltage and load disturbances. The tuning of the PI controller parameter is done using the Ziegler-Nichols method. At last, these studies are verified through MATLAB Simulation.

articleTitle: A Blockchain enabled Auction and Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading System in a Local Energy Market
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The concept of peer-to-peer local energy trading holds the promise of fostering a more sustainable and efficient energy ecosystem, aligning with the global goals of environmental responsibility, energy conservation, and the advancement of renewable energy sources. As such, it has attracted lots of attention from researchers seeking to revolutionize the energy sector and address the challenges associated with traditional centralized energy models. However, to effectively set up a local energy market, two vital components are needed – a robust transaction infrastructure and a welldefined set of market and auction rules. In this paper, our proposed solution relies on the Ethereum blockchain and smart contracts, thereby exploiting the benefits of blockchain technology to meet the requirements for secure and decentralized energy trading within a community, all without the need for a trusted third party. We propose an Ethereumbased framework to facilitate secure and decentralized peer-topeer electricity trading among the members of a smart community. The framework implements smart contract auction with filters at different stages throughout the process to ensure the integrity of data, maintain data confidentiality, and safeguard user identity privacy on the network. We also performed a thorough security assessment of our smart contract using MythX by Consensys - a security analysis tool for Ethereum smart contracts to identify and rectify any potential security threat and vulnerabilities in our proposed framework and auction process.

articleTitle: Solar Power Forecasting using Machine Learning Approaches : A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In recent years, solar energy has rapidly grown in importance as a source of energy in many nations; yet, the short term behavior of Photo Voltaic (PV) power generation has a substantial influence on current power networks. Accurate solar power forecasting techniques are needed to lower this uncertainty and ensure system security. This paper compiles and contrasts several methods for forecasting PV power, including ensemble methods, machine and deep learning methods, time-series statistical methods, physical methods, and methods based on physical principles. The features selection for PV power generation forecasting models is also covered, along with a summary of alternative optimization strategies for model parameters and an investigation of the critical variables that affect PV power forecasts. The many deterministic and probabilistic forecasting models that are currently available are compared in this study. It is projected that probabilistic forecasting will play an important role in the PV power forecasting required to address the issues posed by modern power systems. The significance of data processing methods that improve predicting performance is also emphasized. Compared to previous studies, this study highlights more challenges with applying Deep Learning (DL) to forecast PV power. According to the survey findings, a complete PV power forecasting process must have the ability to analyze data, extract features, train on a potent deep learning framework, and assess the degree of uncertainty in its forecasts.

articleTitle: EV and RE Uncertainty Analysis in Micro-Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Micro-grids have gained significant attention as localized energy systems that incorporate RES (Renewable Energy Sources) and EVs (Electric Vehicles), contributing to enhanced sustainability and resilience. However, the integration of these variable and stochastic components introduces uncertainty to micro-grid operations. This paper presents a comprehensive uncertainty analysis of EV (electric vehicles) and REs (Renewable Energy Sources) in micro-grids. The study begins by developing probabilistic models to characterize the inherent variability in renewable energy generation from sources such as wind and solar. It further discovers the impact of meteorological conditions and geographical location on the uncertainty associated with these resources. Subsequently, the uncertain nature of electric vehicle charging and discharging behaviors is investigated, considering factors like user preferences, charging infrastructure availability, and driving patterns. The paper introduces the LSTM technique for load forecasting in MG (Micro-Grid) operations to assess uncertainty propagation. Several scenarios are investigated in order to assess the dynamic interactions between EVs (Electric Vehicles), RES (Renewable Energy Sources), ESS (Energy Storage Systems) under various uncertainty scenarios. The analysis quantifies the effects of uncertainties on key performance metrics, including energy supply reliability, economic feasibility, and carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Development of Discrete Optimized Periodic Output Feedback Controller for Grid Connected AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Protection of the environment and the shortage of conventional fossil fuels have become the key inspirations to integrate more renewable power generators into power systems. However, high penetration of AC microgrid into the power system may increase the use of power electronic converter interface causing a decrease of overall power system inertia, reduction of available reserve power margin and growing risk of load shedding. Also, the fluctuating nature of power output from the AC microgrid due to the variable nature of power generation causes a severe burden on conventional power generators and such power deviations have a substantial impact on the system stability. This paper examines the effects of the grid-connected AC microgrid on the stability of existing power systems. Power electronics interfaced AC microgrids increase the low-frequency oscillations. To enhance the stability, a discrete mode power oscillation damping controller (PODC) is proposed for grid-connected AC microgrids. A discrete mode PODC is designed to implement the conceptual framework of periodic output feedback (POF) and various sets of input and output sampling time intervals. Both gain and optimal sampling time intervals of the POF controller are determined by utilizing the particle swarm optimization technique. In this consideration, the POF-based discrete controller is a robust power oscillation damping controller that provides distinct benefits compared to conventional power system stabilizers in the damping of low-frequency electromechanical oscillatory modes. The simulation result demonstrates the performance of discrete mode time-domain PODC with optimum control operational gain and sampling time interval under fault conditions and load perturbation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Circuit Breaker Capability for Reignition Free Operation of 400kv Shunt Reactor and 765kv Shunt Reactor with Ngr Using Controlled Switching Device
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The shunt reactor is a key element in the Extra High Voltage (EHV) power system used for voltage regulation. The current drawn by the reactor is highly inductive; due to this feature, it presents constraints in current interruption by circuit breakers. The current can resume after interruption if the rate of rise of dielectric strength (RRDS) of the dielectric medium is lower than the rise time derivative of the recovery voltage and can result in an unsuccessful current interruption. Based on this consideration, minimum arcing time is prescribed by Circuit Breaker (CB) manufacturers. Evaluation of the re-ignition free window for the EHV 420kV 80Mvar shunt reactor has been carried out in this paper as per the procedure laid out in IEC-62271-100 and IEEE-035-017 with the help of PSCAD-EMTDC software package. The results are well supported by field-implemented disturbance records of controlled switching opening operation. The effect of the presence of a surge arrester on Transient Recovery Voltage (TRV) has been considered and elaborated. The effect of the presence of a neutral grounding reactor (NGR) with a 765kV Shunt reactor is also discussed in this paper. The presence of NGR tends to increase the peak of TRV peak and the same has been calculated through simulations, the field results are then discussed based on the re-ignition free window calculated as per IEC 62271–100. Optimum controlled switching helps in the reduction of mechanical and electromagnetic stresses generated during random switching operations of the reactor. The simulation results and field reports are in good agreement and controlled switching helps in meeting the opening targets within a re-ignition free window with fair accuracy.

Author Keywords: Rate of rise of recovery voltage
Rate of rise of dielectric strength

articleTitle: An Adaptive DOCR Coordination for Microgrid Protection using JAYA Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: In the context of modern microgrids, the task of achieving effective relay coordination presents a substantial challenge, mainly due to the changing magnitudes and directions of fault currents. This challenge becomes particularly acute when dealing with inverter-interfaced Distributed Generators (IIDGs) and synchronous-based Distributed Generators (SBDGs). The traditional relay protection scheme proves inadequate in adapting the changes in micro grid topologies and addressing multiple protection issues. Consequently, the attainment of optimal relay coordination becomes indispensable for ensuring robust microgrid protection. The conventional objective function employed in relay coordination encounters issues related to miscoordination and insensitivity. In light of this research paper introduces an optimized coordination approach for directional overcurrent relays (DOCRs) within the microgrids. The proposed method employ the JAYA algorithm in conjunction with a modified objective function. The proposed objective function not only considers coordination time intervals (CTI) but also incorporates factors related to miscoordination and insensitivity. Notably, the JAYA algorithm distinguishes itself from traditional optimization strategies by not necessitating specific control parameters. To gauge the effectiveness of the proposed method, the scheme is tested on a 4-bus radial distribution system, conducting comparative assessments against other contemporary optimization techniques.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Fault Location in Distribution Systems Based on Bayesian Optimised CNN-SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This work proposes a novel, optimized hybrid fault location finding technique in power distribution systems with radial and ring topologies. The transient current signals recorded at each node of the IEEE 13-node test feeder are processed using various convolutional neural network (CNN) designs, including AlexNet, GoogleNet, SqueezeNet, and ResNet. Support vector machines (SVMs) (which identify the nodes and determine where the fault occurs in the IEEE 13-node test feeder) are trained using these features extracted by CNN architectures. Two SVM hyperparameters—the box constraint and kernel scale—are adjusted using Bayesian optimization (BO) to increase the accuracy of fault location. The success of the suggested method is evaluated using many characteristics, including fault type, resistance, inception angle, and nodes. An analysis is done on how four different Kernel functions—polynomial, RBF, Gaussian, and linear—affect the performance of the SVM method. In terms of fault location accuracy, this model's performance is evaluated. By obtaining 100% fault location accuracy for radial topologies and 97.35% for ring topologies of power distribution systems, the simulation results show the utility of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Advancement and Prospects of FACTS Devices in Enhancing India's Power System Stability and Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The integration of FACTS devices into India's power grid infrastructure has steer in a new era of grid management and efficiency. This paper provides a detailed analysis of FACTS devices' historical development, technological functions, and their diverse applications within evolving India's power sector. It explores significant installations & projects that have contributed to a more stable and reliable electrical system. From the pioneering installation of TCSCs on key transmission lines to the deployment of STATCOMs for voltage control & reactive power management, FACTS devices have played a pivotal role in addressing unique challenges of India's power system. This paper also inquiries into the practical benefits of FACTS technology in India, including improved voltage stability and enhanced power flow control. By optimizing grid performance & addressing critical grid management issues, FACTS devices are shaping the future of India's power sector.

articleTitle: The Novel Protocol Uses Low Computational Complexity to Authenticate Edge Devices on Smart Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Grid computing has emerged as a powerful paradigm for harnessing distributed computing resources to solve complex problems. In grid computing, various devices across different administrative domains collaborate to provide computational power and storage capacity. Sensor agent devices have become the backbone of modern technological systems such as Internet of Things (IoT), smart homes, industrial automation, and autonomous vehicles. These devices collect and process real-time data from the surrounding environment, providing crucial insights for decision-making, monitoring, and control purposes. However, the performance of these devices depends on space complexity and time complexity. Achieving optimum performance in sensor agent devices requires a delicate balance between space complexity and time complexity. Reducing one complexity may increase the other, and vice versa. Light weight authentication device-based algorithms play a vital role in verifying the identity of devices and ensuring secure communication within the grid and that needs to satisfy complexity. These protocols verify the identity of devices and users, ensuring that only authorized entities can access and interact with the data. In this article, we will explore a new light weight authentication protocol based on a block cipher i.e ELBC (Extended Linear Block cipher algorithm). The new authentication protocols are easy to implement and deploy in any kind of environment. The algorithm divides the authentication message into blocks and encrypts them using matrix multiplication. By generating an invertible key matrix and applying encryption and decryption equations, the proposed algorithm ensures secure communication.

articleTitle: ML-Based Fault Detection Strategies for Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Power electronics plays a pivotal role in modern energy systems, contributing to improved efficiency, reduced emissions, and enhanced control in various applications such as renewable energy integration, electric vehicles, and smart grids. This vital domain within electrical engineering, has undergone a remarkable transformation through the integration of Machine Learning, as the power electronics industry has witnessed significant advancements in optimizing operations, improving reliability, and enabling sustainable energy solutions. This research paper presents various strategies of Machine learning used in power electronics. It focuses on using Machine Learning based models to examine and train various voltage and current record units obtained by simulated malfunctioning transmission line model created with Matlab /Simulink. This yielded a dataset consisting of 12,001 fault data samples. Machine Learning models SVM, KNN and Decision Tree were trained on the same data and were employed to detect the faults. Next, the model was chosen for its strong fault detection capabilities and potential, which were evaluated based on accuracy, precision, and the F1- score. Effective fault detection techniques play a crucial role in optimizing power system control, reducing energy wastage, and ensuring top-notch performance.

articleTitle: Exploring the Interrelationship of Communication Networks and Human Operators in Power Grid Cascading Failures Through an Integrated Modeling Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: Cascade failures in the electrical grid have been studied extensively; however, most of this work has been done using isolated power system dynamics models. But it has been proven that communication networks and the activities of human operators play key roles in the event of a cascade failure in a modern smart grid. When a smart grid has a cascading failure, this study investigates the intricate feedback loops that occur between the power grid, the underlying communication network, and human operators. Analysis and characterization of cascade failure dynamics using a Markov chain model. The proposed model offers a fresh perspective on how to assess the impact of reliance among these three critical levels on the escalation of cascading failures. With the IEEE 118-bus system, we model and simulate the dynamics of cascading failures in the power grid and show and quantify the effect of communication networks and human operator reactions. Understanding the intricate connection between these variables and the stability and reliability of modern power networks is made easier thanks to the information provided by this study.

articleTitle: Power Management and Control for a Subsea Cable Tied Floating Solar PV-Battery Based Distributed Generation System for Remote Islands
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The use of diesel generators (DG) sets as the central source of power generation can be lowered through supplementing the load requirement through installed renewable energy-based sources. The batteries due to their lower cost, lesser maintenance and storage property helps in reducing the DG set rating or eliminating the DG sets. Thus, remote islands use distributed solar photovoltaic systems and battery storage systems as primary sources of power. Proper power management and coordination between the distributed sources can minimize the use of grid power and help to earn revenue by maximizing the power sold by the renewable sources. The remote systems also face severe power quality issues due to connected electronic loads drawing harmonic dominant currents. Moreover, the presence of harmonics in the grid parameters lead to violation of the standard grid codes leading to penalty to the microgrid operators and the consumers. To reduce the effect of power quality, this work presents a control for better power quality performance of the system comprising of solar and battery storage system for a remote island application. A frequency adaptive pre-filter phase locked loop (FAPF-PLL) based control is deployed to improve the grid power quality indices. The developed power management scheme also regulates the BES to store or sell power to the grid to maximize the revenue based on generation, demand, battery state and tariff. The performance of power management and power quality controls are presented during several extreme conditions through simulation results.

articleTitle: Robust Power Frequency Control for Pumped Storage Hydropower Station
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: This research study explores the impact of Sliding Mode Control (SMC) controllers and pumped storage hydro power stations on the frequency stability of a two-area power system. A comprehensive simulation model is developed to evaluate the system's response to load disturbances. The findings reveal that the implementation of SMC controllers yields significant improvements in frequency stability compared to conventional Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) controllers. The frequency deviation is reduced by an impressive 43%, demonstrating the remarkable effectiveness of SMC controllers in regulating and maintaining system frequency. Furthermore, the integration of pumped storage hydro power stations into the system enhances its frequency response characteristics, resulting in minimized frequency deviations during generating operations. This synergistic combination of SMC controllers and pumped storage units offers a highly promising and robust approach to achieve reliable frequency regulation and mitigate the adverse effects of load disturbances in power systems. These results underscore the vital role of advanced control strategies and renewable energy storage solutions in ensuring a stable, resilient, and sustainable electricity supply.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of a Neutral Point Clamp (NPC) Five -Level-Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper presents that the gross elimination of the harmonics as function of total harmonic distortion (THD) across the load side of the neutral point clamping (NPC) five level-Inverters with single stage LC-filter which plays an important character to preserve the good quality of the power in the power distribution. Flexible sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) control strategy is used for driving the power switches of the proposed NPC converter system to null and void the asymmetrical harmonics with lower rating of semiconductors. Performance assessment and improvement are taken into account by simple modeling, analysis and lower switching power losses of semiconductors while it is applicative for the medium power application

articleTitle: Design Development and Analysis of 3-DOF Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper presents the arm design, kinematics analysis, path planning, and CAD modeling, enabling the practical use of a low-cost robotic arm as a laboratory model for teaching and learning about robots. The arm design is created using Fusion 360 software and features four servo motors as actuators. Kinematics analysis is performed using the Denavit-Hartenberg convention. The proposed framework encompasses a robotic arm with three degrees of freedom (3-DOF) and employs four DC servo motors for each joint's movement. Arm motion control is based on an Arduino control unit, utilizing a Python-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) with a kinematics algorithm in the backend, providing a user-friendly environment for remotely controlling the robot arm's end-effector. The path planning framework is constructed using cubic splines, taking joint restrictions into account. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through RoboAnalyzer simulation results, demonstrating improved motion accuracy, smoothness, and efficiency. Additionally, this robot arm can operate autonomously for pick-and-place applications with the assistance of an Arduino controller.
